chunks: went to visit Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik, but the permission to see him was delayed until he became distressed. Hisham had a gatekeeper who was wealthy in worldly goods but had no children. Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) approached the gatekeeper and said: 'Is there something with you by which you could bring me to Hisham, and I will teach you a supplication by which you will have children?' He said: 'Yes.' So he brought him to Hisham and fulfilled all of his needs.

He said: When he had finished, the gatekeeper said to him: 'May I be your ransom! The supplication you mentioned to me?' He said to him: 'Yes — say each day, in the morning and the evening, "Glory be to God" seventy times, seek forgiveness ten times, glorify nine times, and conclude the tenth with seeking forgiveness. Then recite the Words of God, Mighty and Majestic:

"Ask forgiveness of your Lord, surely He is Most Forgiving. He will send the sky upon you in abundance. And will aid you with wealth and sons, and will make for you gardens, and will make for you rivers." [Quran 71:10-12]
The gatekeeper recited it and was blessed with abundant offspring. And after that, he maintained connection with Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them both).

Sulayman said: So I recited it too — I had married a cousin of mine and a child had been delayed from her — and I taught it to my wife and was blessed with a child. The woman claimed that whenever she desired to become pregnant, she would become pregnant when she recited it. And I taught it to more than one person among the Hashimites who had not been having children, and they were blessed with many children.

key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: A self-sacrificial formula of deep respect — 'May I be your ransom'
key_terms.حَاجِب: Chamberlain, gatekeeper, the officer responsible for controlling access to a caliph
key_terms.مِدْرَار: Continuously pouring, abundant rain — classical Quranic term for divine blessing
key_terms.وَفَدَ: Made a formal visit, traveled to meet (used for ambassadorial delegations)
key_terms.يُولَدُ لَكَ: Passive construction: 'children will be born for you', i.e., 'you will have children'

ai.seo_question: What supplication did Imam al-Baqir teach for having children?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an encounter between Imam al-Baqir (AS) and a gatekeeper of the Umayyad Caliph Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik. When denied prompt entry to Hisham's court, the Imam offered to teach the childless gatekeeper a supplication for fertility in exchange for admittance. The supplication involves glorifications, istighfar (seeking forgiveness), and the recitation of Quran 71:10-12 — the verses of Nuh in which God promises abundance, wealth, children, and rivers to those who persistently seek His forgiveness. The narrator Sulayman confirms its efficacy through personal testimony and corroboration from Hashimites who also received children after practicing it.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Sayyari, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Najran, from Suleyman Bin Ja’far, from Sheykh madany, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having gone to visit Hisham Bin Abdul Malik. So the permission was delayed until it was upsetting, and there was a guard of his who had abundance of the world and he did not have children for him. So Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, approached him, so<sup>asws</sup> he said to him: ‘Is there anything with you which can make me<sup>asws</sup> arrive to Hisham, and I<sup>asws</sup> will teach you a supplication, there would be a birth for you’. He said, ‘Yes’. So he took him<sup>asws</sup> to Hisham, and he<sup>asws</sup> fulfilled all his needs.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So when he<sup>asws</sup> was free, the guard said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you! The supplication which you spoke to me of?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Yes. Say during every day when it is morning and evening, ‘سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ’ ‘Glory be to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’, seventy times, and you should seek Forgiveness ten times, and you should Glorify nine times, and end the tenth with the seeking of the Forgiveness. Then you should be saying the Words of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic

[71:10] So I said, Ask forgiveness of your Lord, surely He is the most Forgiving [71:11] He will send down upon you the cloud, pouring down abundance of rain: [71:12] And Help you with wealth and sons, and Make for you gardens, and Make for you rivers’.
So the guard said it, and was Granted abundant offspring. And after that, he maintained good relations with Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>.

So Suleyman (the narrator) said, ‘So I said it (as well), and I had married a cousin of mine, so the child was delayed upon me from her, and I taught it to my wife, so she gave birth to a child, and the wife (from then on) thought that whenever she so desired to get pregnant, she would do so, when she says it; and I taught it to someone else from the Hashimites, from the ones who did not happen to have children for them, so there were born unto them a lot of children;
and the Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 5. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Sayyariy from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu Najran from Sulayman ibn Ja‘far from a Shaykh from al-Madinah from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Once I wanted to visit Hisham ibn ‘Abd al-Malik but permission for a meeting was delayed and I felt worried.’ He ‘Abd al-Malik had a guard who was wealthy but had no children. Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, asked him, ‘If you can arrange a meeting with Hisham I will teach you a prayer and you will have a child.’ The guard agreed and arranged a meeting between him (the Imam) and Hisham who complied with all that he (the Imam) asked.

When the meeting was over the guard said, T pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, the prayer that you had mentioned.’ He (the Imam) said, ’Everyday in the morning and evening, say seventy times, Tasbih (Allah is free of all defects).’ Then say, T ask forgiveness from Allah, my Lord and return to Him in repentance’ ten times then Tasbih (Allah is free of all defects) nine times and finish the tenth with, T ask forgiveness from Allah, my Lord and return to Him in repentance.’ Then say the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious,
‘Ask forgiveness from your Lord; He is forgiving. He sends you abundant rain from the sky. He helps you by means of your wealth and sons. He makes for you gardens and canals.’ [71:12]
The guard followed the instruction and he was granted a great many children. He thereafter kept good relations with abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam.

Sulayman has said, ‘I also said those prayers and I had married the daughter of my uncle but there was a delay in the birth of a son for me from her. I taught her also the prayer; then a son was born to me and the woman believed that whenever she wanted she could become pregnant after saying the prayer. I taught to more than one person of banu Hashim who did not have children: then many children were born to them.
